title: Synthetic consumption scenarios playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This playbook documents a standardized approach for generating, running, and interpreting synthetic consumption scenarios to evaluate SLA sensitivity, cost exposure, and fidelity degradation risk across Redwood’s deployment surfaces (hosted, dedicated, private). It complements the lab-driven experiments used by Research and the developer sandbox artifacts used by DX. The goal is to create reproducible scenario artifacts and a lightweight simulation harness that product, SRE, and sales engineers can use during onboarding, capacity planning, and pricing negotiations.

Scope and intended audiences

- Scope: scenarios that exercise per-token cost, tail-latency SLOs (P95/P99), KV cache hit-rate dynamics, and fallback behaviors for multi-variant routing. Includes synthetic traffic, session-based conversational traces, and embedding spike simulations.
- Audiences: product managers, solutions engineers, SREs, pricing analysts, and field sales engineers.

Why synthetic scenarios matter

1. Surface non-linear cost behaviors caused by batching, prefix reuse, and KV cache churn.
2. Validate fallback economics when primary variants are preempted or out of capacity.
3. Provide deterministic inputs for pricing simulations and contractual SLA sizing.

Core components of the playbook

1) Scenario Catalog (canonical set)

- conversational-burst: short interactive sessions with high-turn counts (10–50 turns) per session; 80% of sessions are under 2s target latency; median tokens per turn: 64; use-case: chat assistants.
- transactional-hf: high-frequency single-turn calls with small prompts and strict P95 <= 200ms; tokens per request: 8–32; use-case: realtime search rerank and LLM-assisted autocompletion.
- longform-stream: single long responses streamed in chunks; typical response length: 1024–4096 tokens; use-case: summarization and content generation.
- embedding-spike: sudden burst of batched embedding creation (10k–100k vectors) lasting 5–30 minutes; use-case: reindexing and bulk ingestion.
- mixed-fidelity: mixture of high-fidelity (e.g., large variant) and low-fidelity calls with weighted routing to test fallback economics.

Each scenario artifact includes: synthetic traffic generator configuration (load shape, percentiles), seed prompt sets (10–100 canonical prompts), and an acceptance checklist.

2) Metrics and SLO mappings

- Latency: P50, P95, P99, tail-latency spikes (5-min windows). SLO targets: transactional-hf P95 <= 200ms (hosted), conversational-burst P95 <= 500ms (dedicated SLA tier).
- Cost: tokens-per-minute / effective $/1M tokens at current SKU rates. Include delta when fallback to lower-cost variants occurs.
- Quality: BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity vs baseline prompts; pass/fail thresholds for quality gates (e.g., semantic-similarity >= 0.87).
- Cache: KV-cache hit rate, prefix reuse %, and eviction rate per 5-min window.
- Availability: percent successful responses and defined error budget consumption over scenario window.

3) Simulation methodology (step-by-step)

1. Select scenario artifact from the Catalog.
2. Pin model variants and runtime knobs (batch size, max tokens, quantization profile) in the config table below.
3. Run a dry-run at 5–10% scale to validate traffic generator and telemetry hooks.
4. Execute the full-scale run for a minimum of 60 minutes (recommended 3 hours for longer steady-state metrics).
5. Run a correlated quality evaluation on sampled outputs (sample size: 500 responses).
6. Produce the scenario report and SLA sensitivity matrix.

4) Recommended configuration table (canonical defaults)

| parameter | hosted default | dedicated default | rationale |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| request_batch_size | 8 | 32 | Dedicated pools can group larger batches to increase throughput |
| quantization | int8 | int8 | Cost-forward default; evaluate quality gates post-run |
| kv_cache_enabled | true | true | Preserves session prefix reuse economics |
| prefetch_window_ms | 50 | 30 | Lower for dedicated to favor throughput |
| fallback_policy | variant-priority | variant-priority-with-regional-fallthrough | Provide more resilience for dedicated customers |
| telemetry_sample_rate | 1.0 | 1.0 | Full sampling for scenario runs; reduce for production |

5) Acceptance checklist for scenario artifacts

- [ ] Traffic generator validated with dry-run.
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards defined and linked (latency, cost, cache, quality).
- [ ] Sampling seed and randomization seeds recorded in artifact.
- [ ] Reproducibility steps logged (config hash, runtime commit).
- [ ] Quality gate pass for sampled outputs.

6) SLA sensitivity matrix (examples)

- transactional-hf: increasing concurrency from 100 to 1000 at fixed per-request tokens increases P95 from 120ms to 410ms and increases cost by +18% due to smaller batch efficiency; recommend adjusting batch sizing or reserving warm capacity at concurrency > 600.
- conversational-burst: introducing 25% session churn (frequent session creation) drops KV hit rate from 78% to 42%, increasing median token cost by 12% and P99 by 90ms; mitigation: session locality routing and sticky cache anchors.

7) Common experiments and what they reveal

- Quantization toggles: toggling int8->float16 for select variants to quantify quality delta vs cost savings.
- Batch shape sensitivity: sweep batch sizes and request shapes to identify knee points in latency vs throughput.
- Fallback pressure test: simulate full-capacity of primary variant and enable regional fallthrough to measure failover latency and cross-variant quality impact.
- Cold-start warmup: measure latency and token overhead for model cold starts across dedicated pools after 15m idle.

8) Runbook: interpreting results and recommended actions

1. If P95 breaches target but cost remains low, tune batch sizing and prefetch_window_ms.
2. If cost spikes while latency is stable, inspect KV eviction rate and prefix churn—consider increasing cache TTL for long sessions.
3. If quality gates fail after quantization, rollback quantization profile for the affected variant and open a quality regression issue with Model Onboarding team.

9) Ownership and cadence

- Scenario artifacts: owner = Product Experiments (product-experiments@redwood.com).
- Lab runs and long-duration tests: owner = Applied ML & Evals.
- SRE checks and capacity recommendations: owner = eng-sre.

Quarterly cadence: catalog refresh and re-run of top 5 scenarios aligned with pricing reviews and major model variant changes.

10) Telemetry and dashboard recipes (examples)

- Dashboard: consumption-sim-ops (Grafana) – panels: P95 latency, P99 latency, token-rate, cost-rate, KV hit rate, error-rate.
- Query examples (PromQL-like pseudocode):
  - p95_latency = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
  - kv_hit_rate = rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m]) / rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m])

11) Artifact template and CLI snippet

- artifact.yaml (minimal):
  name: conversational-burst-2027-03-run
  scenario: conversational-burst
  seed_prompts: ./seeds/conversational-burst/seed-100.jsonl
  traffic_shape: {rps: 120, burst_profile: exponential, duration_mins: 180}
  variants: [gptx-large-v1-quant, gptx-small-v1-quant]
  knobs: {batch_size: 16, kv_cache_enabled: true, telemetry_sample_rate: 1.0}

- Run (local harness):
  ./sim-harness run --artifact artifact.yaml --telemetry destination=grafana/consumption-sim-ops --commit $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)

Appendix A — Example scenario report outline

- Executive summary (1 paragraph)
- Key findings (bulleted)
- SLA sensitivity matrix (table)
- Cost delta summary ($/1M tokens baseline vs observed)
- Quality sample notes and failing prompts
- Recommended mitigations and owners

Appendix B — Troubleshooting tips

- Partial telemetry: verify telemetry_sample_rate and OTEL exporter configuration.
- Non-reproducible noise: lock random seeds and verify artifact.yaml commit hash.
- Unexpected quality drift: compare outputs against golden baseline and open a Model Onboarding ticket with evidence.

Contact and next steps

For help running scenarios or onboarding scenario artifacts into the catalog, contact product-experiments@redwood.com. The catalog is reviewed quarterly—submit new scenario proposals as PRs to the canonical git repo (internal) with a triage note and a representative seed set.
